accent.note: Graphics duty only, 3.20:1 on the plate. Means the loop and nothing else.

accent-strong.note: Carries white text at 5.12:1. A/B markers and nudger chips.

accent-text.note: Accent-coloured text: 5.10:1 on plate, 4.64:1 on well.

accent-wash.note: The armed span tint. Paints behind the timeline bars, never over them.

surface-plate.note: The ground for every screen, the browser theme-color, and the popover.

surface-raised.note: The lit top of a light cap; hover and keyboard-highlight on an index row.

surface-well.note: Every recess. The binding surface for text contrast in this system.

surface-well-deep.note: A recess inside a recess: switch track off, disarmed chip, disabled action.

surface-edge.note: The 1px hairline that makes every structural edge. Most-used token in the build.

surface-rule.note: The hairline between peers. Same value as Deep Well; a separate role because a divider and a recess floor change independently.

ink.note: All primary text (10.66:1 on the well), played bars, playhead, focus ring, ::selection, alert ground.

ink-body.note: Secondary text at 5.78:1 on the well.

ink-label.note: The floor for text in this system, at 5.02:1 on the well. Nothing quieter carries text.

ink-inverse.note: Text on ink: the alert chip, the held key. 12.56:1.

cap-top.note: Upper stop of the dark cap gradient.

cap-bottom.note: Lower stop of the dark cap gradient.

cap-ink.note: The mark on a dark cap, at 9.51:1.

cap-edge.note: The shadow colour a cap sits in. Declared but unreferenced; its value is in live use as a literal inside the three shadow tokens.

timeline-bar.note: An unplayed graduation, 3.11:1 against the well.

timeline-bar-in-loop.note: An unplayed graduation inside the armed span: 3.04:1 against the washed ground, 3.10:1 against the played bar.

on-accent.note: Marks and text sitting on an accent surface: the A/B markers and armed nudger chips, 5.12:1 over accent-strong. Exists so no component carries a raw #ffffff.

surface-hi.note: Only ever the top stop of a hovered light cap's gradient. A lift, not a surface: nothing is filled with it.

position.purpose: The playback position, tabular, top-left of the recessed panel. The single largest object on any screen; nothing else is set at either size.

view-title.purpose: The h1 on Connect and Start.

track-title.purpose: What is loaded, in the now-playing header. Deliberately a step below Position: what you are playing, not what you are working on.

readout.purpose: The A and B times in the nudger rows. Inverted: smaller on desktop, where the row is compact. Flagged in Open as possibly not a real step.

brand.purpose: 'Rewindify' in every header. Inverted: smaller on desktop, where it sits in a dense 56px chassis.

body.purpose: Explanatory copy and the artist line, in Body Ink. Its smallest step is 13px, at the alert chips and the desktop search input.

row-title.purpose: Track titles in the printed index. Steps with the row size prop, not the breakpoint: 13px at sm, 15px at lg.

figure.purpose: Every quantity that is not Position or Readout. A band, not one step: 14/13px beside the position, 12px at the loop range and row durations, 11px at the smaller variants and A/B markers, 10px at keycaps and phone tick labels.

meta.purpose: Album, session name, loop hint, empty-state text. 11px at the credit line.

legend.purpose: The legend() mixin. Printed nomenclature; the only small type in the system. One exception: legend(11px) on the callback screen.

shadows.name: well
shadows.purpose: Anything cut into the plate: panels, inputs, artwork, the active index row, the switch track. Edge ring and depth in one declaration.

shadows.name: cap
shadows.purpose: Any raised pressable control. The white inset highlight along the top edge is what makes it read as lit rather than as a card.

shadows.name: cap-pressed
shadows.purpose: The :active state of a dark cap, paired with translateY(1px).

shadows.name: key-held
shadows.purpose: A held A/B keycap. Same convention as cap-pressed, one step deeper, because a held key is pressed and stays pressed rather than momentarily.

shadows.name: cap-light
shadows.purpose: A raised light control: secondary actions that must not read as primary.

shadows.name: cap-light-pressed
shadows.purpose: The :active state of a light cap.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: The desktop search results plate, and nothing else. Exactly one thing in this product leaves the surface.

shadows.name: hairline-edge
shadows.purpose: Every structural edge in the product. Direction and axis vary; the mechanism never does. Never a CSS border.

shadows.name: hairline-rule
shadows.purpose: The divider between peers: index rows, list headers.

shadows.name: popover-flush
shadows.purpose: The popover before it has left the plate. The closed end of the lift, same two layers so the pair interpolates one-to-one.

shadows.name: knockout
shadows.purpose: A 1px hard ring of the surrounding surface, printed to give a mark an edge against whatever it lands on. A print device, not depth, which is why it is exempt from the Offset-Plus-Blur Rule.

shadows.name: cap-light-held
shadows.purpose: A sustained press on a light cap: the passages handle for as long as its drawer is open. One step past the momentary press, because at press depth a state that persists does not read as a state.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The system's only easing curve. Exponential, not a linear fade.

motion.name: arm-duration
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: arming the loop sweeps the span open from its centre. Zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: press-duration
motion.purpose: A cap press. Everything not the loop arming is either this or instant. Zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: grip-delay
motion.purpose: The A/B grips fade in behind the span sweep.

motion.name: lift-duration
motion.purpose: Two cap presses (220ms). The search popover leaving its slot, and the passages drawer opening. Derived rather than declared so prefers-reduced-motion still zeroes it.

hair.purpose: Timeline bars only, so a 1px graduation is not a hard rectangle.

tight.purpose: Printed-on things: A/B markers and chips, keycaps, the artwork recess, the search clear button.

default.purpose: Every control and every recess unless stated otherwise. The system's resting radius.

panel.purpose: The one recessed working panel on each layout, and the search popover.

pill.purpose: True circles only: transport keys, playhead knob, switch knob, the Connect placeholder disc.

switch-track-vertical.purpose: Derived, not chosen: half the 26px width of the phone's vertical switch track — the short axis, the one the knob's diameter fills. See the Half-Height Pill Rule.

switch-track-horizontal.purpose: Derived, not chosen: half the 18px height of the horizontal switch track, used at every width where the switch's bay is one row tall. See the Half-Height Pill Rule.

components.name: Transport Key
components.description: The dark raised cap. Three identical circles, because a transport row on real gear has equal keys and stepping back is the most frequent action in a practice session.
components.css: .ds-key-transport { width: 60px; height: 60px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 2px; border: 0; cursor: pointer; border-radius: 50%; background: linear-gradient(var(--cap-top, #3d3d38), var(--cap-bottom, #2a2a27)); color: var(--cap-ink, #f2efe8); box-shadow: 0 1px 1px rgba(31,31,29,0.3), 0 2px 5px rgba(31,31,29,0.16), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.13); transition: box-shadow 110ms ease, transform 110ms ease; } .ds-key-transport__step { font: 500 10px/1 'Archivo Variable', Archivo, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.01em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-feature-settings: 'tnum' 1; color: rgba(242,239,232,0.62); } .ds-key-transport:hover { background: linear-gradient(#474741, var(--cap-top, #3d3d38)); } .ds-key-transport:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--surface-raised, #f4f1ea); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-key-transport:active { transform: translateY(1px); box-shadow: 0 1px 1px rgba(31,31,29,0.34), inset 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.34); }

components.name: Nudge Key
components.description: The raised light cap: a secondary action that must not read as primary. 40px square on the phone because the user is holding an instrument. The row it sits in prints no nomenclature: `LOOP START` / `LOOP END` on a dotted leader were removed to make room for the switch's cell, and the key's own accessible name ("Nudge A back 1 second") is what still speaks the end in full.
components.css: .ds-key-light { width: 40px; height: 40px; display: grid; place-items: center; border: 0; cursor: pointer; border-radius: 3px; background: linear-gradient(var(--surface-raised, #f4f1ea), var(--surface-plate, #ede9e2)); color: var(--ink, #2b2b2a); box-shadow: 0 1px 1px rgba(88,80,64,0.16), 0 2px 4px rgba(88,80,64,0.1), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--surface-edge, #d3cec2); transition: box-shadow 110ms ease, transform 110ms ease; } .ds-key-light:hover { background: linear-gradient(#ffffff, var(--surface-raised, #f4f1ea)); } .ds-key-light:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink, #2b2b2a); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-key-light:active { transform: translateY(1px); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 3px rgba(88,80,64,0.26), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--surface-edge, #d3cec2); }

components.name: Primary Action
components.description: A full-width dark cap for the one committing action on a screen. The neutral disc is a placeholder slot for Spotify's official mark and must never become an invented mark.
components.css: .ds-action { width: 100%; max-width: 420px; height: 50px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 10px; border: 0; cursor: pointer; border-radius: 3px; background: linear-gradient(var(--cap-top, #3d3d38), var(--cap-bottom, #2a2a27)); color: var(--cap-ink, #f2efe8); box-shadow: 0 1px 1px rgba(31,31,29,0.3), 0 2px 5px rgba(31,31,29,0.16), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.13); transition: box-shadow 110ms ease, transform 110ms ease; } .ds-action__mark { width: 14px; height: 14px; flex: none; border-radius: 50%; background: currentcolor; opacity: 0.55; } .ds-action__label { font: 600 14px/1 'Archivo Variable', Archivo, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.005em; } .ds-action:hover { background: linear-gradient(#474741, var(--cap-top, #3d3d38)); } .ds-action:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--surface-raised, #f4f1ea); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-action:active { transform: translateY(1px); box-shadow: 0 1px 1px rgba(31,31,29,0.34), inset 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.34); }

components.name: Search Field
components.description: A recess cut into the plate. No border, no outline: the well is the field. The drawn search mark leads in Label Ink.
components.css: .ds-field { width: 320px; height: 34px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 0 9px; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--surface-well, #e3dfd6); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgba(88,80,64,0.16), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--surface-edge, #d3cec2); } .ds-field__icon { flex: none; color: var(--ink-label, #5f5c55); } .ds-field__input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; background: none; border: 0; outline: none; color: var(--ink, #2b2b2a); font: 400 13px/1.2 'Archivo Variable', Archivo, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-field__input::placeholder { color: var(--ink-label, #5f5c55); } .ds-field:focus-within { box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgba(88,80,64,0.16), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--surface-edge, #d3cec2), 0 0 0 2px var(--ink, #2b2b2a); }

components.name: Index Row
components.description: A printed index, not a stack of cards. Hairline rules between siblings; a dotted leader carries the title to its duration; the loaded track becomes a recess.
components.css: .ds-index { width: 300px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; font-family: 'Archivo Variable', Archivo, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-row { width: 100%; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 11px; padding: 9px 14px; border: 0; cursor: pointer; text-align: left; background: transparent; border-radius: 3px; } .ds-row + .ds-row { box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 var(--surface-rule, #dcd7cc); } .ds-row.is-active { background: var(--surface-well, #e3dfd6); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgba(88,80,64,0.16), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--surface-edge, #d3cec2); } .ds-row:not(.is-active):hover { background: var(--surface-raised, #f4f1ea); } .ds-row:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink, #2b2b2a); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-row__art { flex: none; width: 40px; height: 40px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--surface-well, #e3dfd6); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgba(88,80,64,0.16), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--surface-edge, #d3cec2); } .ds-row__body { flex: 1; min-width: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 3px; } .ds-row__line { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; min-width: 0; } .ds-row__title { flex: none; max-width: 100%; overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.006em; color: var(--ink, #2b2b2a); } .ds-row__leader { flex: 1; min-width: 10px; border-bottom: 1px dotted var(--surface-edge, #d3cec2); transform: translateY(-3px); } .ds-row__duration { flex: none; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--ink-label, #5f5c55); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-feature-settings: 'tnum' 1; } .ds-row__artist { flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis; font-size: 12px; color: var(--ink-body, #55534d); } .ds-row__ago { flex: none; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--ink-label, #5f5c55); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-feature-settings: 'tnum' 1; }

components.name: Loop Switch
components.description: The only place the accent is allowed to arm, and the system's one compound recess: a well cut into a well. It is a cell in the nudger's band everywhere, and its orientation follows the bay rather than the breakpoint — two forms, not three. Left: the stacked phone, where the bay spans both A/B rows, so the track runs up it at 26×68 — knob down when off, up when armed, the word printed at the end the knob rests at. Right: wherever the bay is one row tall (the wide band and desktop alike), the track lies down at 34×18 with the word above it. That horizontal track is under 40px, and is exempt from the phone-affordance floor for the reason the floor exists: the switch is the mechanism inside the button, and the bay is 56px by 52–54px. The armed track takes `accent-strong` at both sizes because it is measured against the well, where `accent` is only 2.91:1 — the same value the A/B chips beside it take, for the same reason.
components.css: .ds-loop { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: 0; cursor: pointer; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--surface-well, #e3dfd6); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgba(88,80,64,0.16), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--surface-edge, #d3cec2); } .ds-loop__label { font: 600 10px/1 'Archivo Variable', Archivo, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.09em; } .ds-loop.is-on .ds-loop__switch { background: var(--accent-strong, #c24309); } .ds-loop__knob { position: absolute; left: 3px; border-radius: 50%; background: linear-gradient(var(--cap-top, #3d3d38), var(--cap-bottom, #2a2a27)); box-shadow: 0 1px 1px rgba(31,31,29,0.3), 0 2px 5px rgba(31,31,29,0.16), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.13); } .ds-loop--tall { align-self: stretch; gap: 8px; padding: 12px 11px; } .ds-loop--tall .ds-loop__switch { width: 26px; } .ds-loop--flat { gap: 7px; height: 52px; padding: 0 11px; } .ds-loop--flat .ds-loop__switch { width: 34px; height: 18px; border-radius: 9px; } .ds-loop--flat .ds-loop__knob { top: 3px; width: 12px; } .ds-loop:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink, #2b2b2a); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Loop Point Chip
components.description: The signature chip, drawn at two scales so the timeline marker and the nudger row read as one control. Takes the accent only while the loop is armed.
components.html: ABAB
components.css: .ds-chip { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; flex: none; width: 24px; height: 20px; border-radius: 2px; font: 700 12px/1 'Archivo Variable', Archivo, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.02em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-feature-settings: 'tnum' 1; background: var(--surface-well-deep, #dcd7cc); color: var(--ink-label, #5f5c55); transition: background-color 320ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), color 320ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-chip.is-armed { background: var(--accent-strong, #c24309); color: #ffffff; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(31,31,29,0.28); }

components.name: Alert Chip
components.description: The whole alert register: inverted ink with the drawn alert mark. There is no red in this system, because the accent means the loop and the next strongest signal is ink.
components.html: Playback moved to another Spotify device.
components.css: .ds-alert { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; margin: 0; padding: 11px 13px; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--ink, #2b2b2a); color: var(--ink-inverse, #f4f1ea); font: 400 13px/1.3 'Archivo Variable', Archivo, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-alert svg { flex: none; }

components.name: Keycap
components.description: Keyboard legends screened onto the engraved chassis strip. The held state inverts to ink and presses down, because holding A or B is a real machine state.
components.html: SPACEPlayAB+←→Move loop

components.name: Passages Handle
components.description: The drawer's handle. The only light cap with a sustained pressed state: a cap whose drawer is open is pressed and stays pressed. The loop switch used to share its phone band and its label register; the switch is a recess in the nudger at both steps now, so this is the only control in that band on the phone and the controls row's one right-anchored control on desktop. Prints its count, because that figure is the only thing telling a shut drawer from an empty one.

narrative.overview:
Rewindify is practice hardware, not a media player. It presents as one warm machined plate with things cut into it, things raised off it, and things printed on it — the visual grammar of Braun product graphics rather than of a streaming app. The category ships dark rounded cards floating over blurred cover art; this system refuses that outright. There is one plate, one ink, and one orange, and the orange means the loop.

The density is instrument density: exact quantities, generous tap targets, and no ornament competing with the one number the user came to read. The position readout is the largest object on the surface at 64px (46px on the phone) because the story is a musician holding an instrument who glances once, reads the exact position, steps back five seconds, and pins the passage as a loop. Everything downstream of that glance — the waveform timeline, the equal-weight step keys, the printed recently-played index — is arranged so nothing has to be hunted for.

Depth is real but shallow, the way a panel is. Surfaces are wells (recessed), caps (raised, pressable, dark), or print (labels and hairline rules). Nothing floats except the one popover, and nothing is outlined. The system is built to switch to an anthracite plate by redefining one token block, which is why no consumer anywhere reads a hex value.
keyCharacteristics: One warm plate (#EDE9E2), one ink (#2B2B2A), one rationed orange (#E2510F).
Every edge is a recess, a raised cap, or a 1px hairline. There are no outlined boxes.
Archivo throughout, with tabular figures on every quantity and no monospace anywhere.
One icon family (Phosphor) on one 256-unit grid at two weights only; no glyph or Unicode stand-ins.
One authored motion moment (arming the loop), and one subordinate one at press speed (the popover leaving the plate). No position value is ever eased.
Keyboard-complete at both breakpoints; neither is the degraded case.
Role-named tokens only, so a second plate is a token swap and not a refactor.

rules.name: The One Orange Rule
rules.body: accent, accent-strong, accent-text and accent-wash are one hue split by contrast duty, and they mean the loop. Nothing else on any surface may take orange — not a play button, not a link, not a brand mark, not a chart, not an error. This is why playback failures use an inverted-ink chip instead of red, why the focus ring is ink, and why ::selection is ink. If a new element wants the accent, the question to answer first is whether it is the loop.

rules.name: The Ink Alert Rule
rules.body: The alert register is inverted ink: ink ground, ink-inverse text, 3px radius, with the Phosphor alert mark. There is no red, amber or green in this system, and adding one would be a second colour with a meaning — which is what the One Orange Rule exists to prevent.

rules.name: The Reserved Band Rule
rules.body: No generated, placeholder or decorative fill may land in HSL hue 5–45°, the band the accent occupies (#E2510F is ~19°). src/fake/catalogue.ts constrains fixture artwork to 70–300° for exactly this reason, and computes its inner disc as hue + 40 so neither the ground nor the disc can wrap into the band. Any future generated imagery inherits this constraint.

rules.name: The Floor Rule
rules.body: The well, not the plate, is the binding surface: tick labels, legends, durations and the A/B times all sit on it. ink-label at 5.02:1 there is the floor. A new text colour earns its place by measurement on the well, not by looking about right on the plate.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every figure the user reads as a quantity carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums and font-feature-settings: 'tnum' 1, applied through the figures() mixin and globally to input, output, time and kbd. Quantities never shift width as they tick. The corollary is absolute: no monospace face anywhere — the grotesque's own tabular figures do this job, and a mono face would read as a code editor, not an instrument.

rules.name: The Printed Legend Rule
rules.body: Small text is set through legend() — bold, tracked, uppercase, Label Ink — or it is not set small. There is no 10px sentence case in this system. Legends may be carried to their value on a dotted leader (surface-edge, 1px, dotted), the way a printed index carries a title to its duration.

rules.name: The One Numeral Rule
rules.body: Position is set larger than the track title, always. The build this replaced had a 20px clock beside a 22px title and consequently no focal point at all. The rule binds every screen that prints a position, which is why the Gate Title can take the same pair without breaking it: a screen with no position readout has no numeral for a heading to outrank. A second heading at those steps, on a screen that does carry a position, is the thing this rule exists to stop.

rules.name: The Two Steps Rule
rules.body: A role has exactly two steps, a desktop step and a phone step — never a fluid clamp() or a vw term, and never a third size invented for the wide band. Three bands, two steps: the wide band picks one of the pair per role, it does not interpolate. A new size that is not one of the 15 documented steps is drift, and a new role must declare both of its steps before it ships.

rules.name: The Inverted Pair Rule
rules.body: Exactly two roles get smaller on desktop rather than larger: Brand (17→15) and Readout (18→16). Both sit in dense desktop chrome — a 56px header and a compact 52px nudger row — where the phone gives them a whole column. Every other role scales up. A third inversion needs a reason of the same kind, or it is a mistake.

rules.name: The Single Source Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: Both boundaries live in SCSS and are exported to TS. Never hard-code a media query width in a component, and never restate a boundary in JavaScript — useIsDesktop() and useIsWide() read them from the stylesheet. A band belongs in JS only for a quantity CSS cannot reach, which today is one: the artwork edge in the now-playing header.

rules.name: The Keyboard Parity Rule
rules.body: src/composables/usePlayerKeyboard.ts is mounted by both player views. Space, arrow-step, L, S, and A/B-hold nudge work at every width; the phone layout is not the degraded case. A phone-width window is not necessarily a touch-only one, and the primary user's hands are on an instrument. Any new control that gains a keyboard path gains it in the shared composable, not in one view.

rules.name: The Three Edges Rule
rules.body: well(), cap() and cap-light() in src/styles/surfaces.scss are the only ways to make an edge, alongside a printed hairline. There are no outlined boxes in this system — no border: 1px solid, no card outline, no ring. This one constraint is what makes eleven components and five views read as a single machined surface, and it is the first thing an accidental change will break.

rules.name: The Offset-Plus-Blur Rule
rules.body: Every shadow that carries depth has a vertical offset. A zero-offset halo (0 0 Npx, blurred) is a glow, belongs to a different world, and is not used here. A zero-offset, zero-blur spread (0 0 0 1px) is the Knockout above and is exempt — it draws an edge, not a light — which is why --shadow-well has always contained one.

rules.name: The One Popover Rule
rules.body: Exactly one thing in this product leaves the surface: the desktop search results, anchored with CSS anchor positioning (anchor-name, position-area, position-try-fallbacks: flip-block) and rendered on a plate-coloured ground. Everything else is in the plate. A second floating layer would break the "one panel" reading.

rules.name: The Half-Height Pill Rule
rules.body: A track that a knob rides in takes a radius of half its own height, rounded up — never a fixed step from the radius scale and never 9999px. The loop switch is the only such track today, at both its sizes: 28px tall → 14px, 25px tall → 13px (12.5 rounded up). Those two values are therefore derived, not chosen; resize the track and the radius follows it. A true circle uses 50% instead.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: New icons come from Phosphor, are named by what the app calls them, and are added to the map in AppIcon.vue — never imported at the call site, so the name-to-glyph decision stays in one file. They take fill only if they are transport marks, and regular otherwise; a third weight, a second icon package, or a glyph like » or ▶ shipped as an icon breaks the set — the whole point is that a step key and a search field read as parts of one machine.

rules.name: The Say-It-Once Rule
rules.body: Every quantity on the player has exactly one printed home, and it is the element that owns the value. Position is the readout, and only there. The track's extent is the small figure beside it. A and B are the nudger rows, because that is where they are changed. The track's shape in time is the printed scale, which labels at most five graduations and leaves the rest as minor marks. Everything the loop draws on the timeline — the wash, the bracket, the two markers — is a graphic statement of A and B, not a second printed one, which is the only reason it does not violate this rule.

rules.name: The Frequency Sets Material Rule
rules.body: A control's material states how often it is pressed. A dark cap is a thing you press constantly (transport, "Continue with Spotify"); a light cap is a thing you press often (nudge keys, search); print is a thing you press almost never. Sign out is the rarest action in the product, and it shipped for a while as a 122px light cap carrying an eject mark — heavier than the brand beside it, and on the phone a matched twin of the search cap, so the header read as two controls of equal standing when one of them is used every session and the other once. It is now a printed legend() word with the anchor hairline from base.scss under it, and its hit box is bought with min-height the rule never sees: text-decoration paints under the glyphs, not under the box, so the word stays print while the target clears 44px on the phone. A new header action earns a cap by naming how often it is pressed.

rules.name: The Unmistakable Verb Rule
rules.body: Copy names the action in the word that cannot be misread on this surface, even when the codebase has a shorter one. The sign-out control says "Sign out" while the store method stays session.disconnect(), because this browser registers as a Spotify Connect playback device — so "Disconnect" has a second, wrong reading available here and nowhere else in the vocabulary. An × was tried first and was worse than either word: a mark next to an account name can mean sign out, remove the account, or dismiss the header, and nothing on the surface picks one.

rules.name: The One Variable Per Channel Rule
rules.body: On the timeline, bar tone carries played-versus-unplayed and the accent carries the loop — through the span wash, the bracket, the A/B markers, the nudger chips, the switch label and the switch. Painting played bars accent inside the span was tried and reverted: it collapsed played against unplayed to 1.24:1, making progress through the passage the least readable thing on screen in the one region this product exists for. Never give one channel two jobs.

rules.name: The Wash Behind Bars Rule
rules.body: .timeline__region must precede .timeline__bars in the template, so the span wash paints behind the bars. As a later sibling it tinted every bar it covered, and no bar tone could then clear 3:1 against both the washed ground and the played bar — the window was shut by 7%. Behind the bars, both pairs clear: played/unplayed 3.10:1, unplayed/ground 3.06:1. Reordering those two elements is a silent accessibility regression. The tint is what this rule binds; .timeline__brace is a separate element that deliberately paints above the bars, because it tints nothing.

rules.name: The Clear Ground Rule
rules.body: Nothing the loop has to print may rely on ground the waveform occupies. Every warm neutral in this system is within a few percent of every other, so no ground-level device can carry a signal on the field at all: the wash caps at 1.13:1 against the well, a deeper well floor at 1.06:1, and orange over an unplayed bar at 1.07:1. The bars are mirrored about the centre line, so the field's top and bottom few pixels — plus the knob strip and the scale strip either side of it — are bare well almost everywhere, and that is where the rails, the boundary rules and their overshoots go. A new loop mark on the timeline earns its place by naming the ground it is measured against, and if that ground is a bar, it needs a gutter or a knockout of its own.

rules.name: The Fabricated Waveform Rule
rules.body: The field is drawn to read as an audio waveform, and it is not one. Spotify exposes no sample data, so src/playback/waveform.ts fabricates the shape from a hash of the track id alone. This is a deliberate, recorded trade: the surface is a portfolio piece and the waveform is what makes it read as practice software, so the honesty cost is accepted here and nowhere else. What makes the fake work is correlation at three scales — an arrangement of four to seven sections at distinct levels, phrase drift from summed octaves of value noise, and asymmetric per-bin scatter with sparse transients. Independent per-bar noise, which the field carried before, reads as broken rather than as audio. The field carries no periodic beat accent: one bar spans several beats at this pitch, and a beat grid would read as a pattern rather than as audio. Tests in src/playback/__tests__/playback.spec.ts hold the three scales: thirds of the field must diverge (arrangement), the mean step between neighbours must stay under a quarter of the field's spread (correlation), and both ends must open on air. Nothing in the interface may claim the shape is the track's audio, and no reading of it is offered as information — it is scenery around an exact position readout.

rules.name: The One Authored Moment Rule
rules.body: Arming the loop is the only designed motion in the build: the span and both bracket rails sweep open from their centre together (transform: scaleX(0 → 1) plus opacity) over --arm-duration (320ms) on --ease-out (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), exponential, not a linear fade), and the boundary rules and grips fade in 120ms behind them. The armed row's rail in the passages drawer sweeps with them, from its own centre on the same tokens — the gesture is the loop's, not the timeline's, so it reaches wherever the loop is stated. Anything the loop adds anywhere joins this sweep rather than getting a moment of its own, which is why applying a saved passage lights the bracket, the nudger chips, the switch label and the row as one event. The region is mounted whether or not the loop is on, so the span sweeps rather than appears. Everything else is instant, a 110ms cap press, or derived from those two tokens by arithmetic — see the rule below. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce zeroes both durations at :root, which disables every transition in the system at once. New motion must be expressed through these two tokens, or through a calc() on one of them, so it inherits that; a component may name such a derivation locally (--lift-duration: calc(var(--press-duration) * 2)) but may not declare a duration of its own, because a literal 220ms would survive reduce and nothing would catch it.

rules.name: The Plate Leaves The Slot Rule
rules.body: The search popover is the only thing in this product that leaves the plate, and it earns motion for exactly that reason: the fact was asserted by a shadow and contradicted by a teleport. It is drawn down out of the slot the search field is cut into — clip-path revealing from the anchored top edge, a 6px translate down, and the shadow rising Popover Flush → Popover — over --lift-duration (two cap presses, 220ms) on --ease-out, exiting in one press at 110ms. Three properties saying one thing.

rules.name: The Never-Eased Position Rule
rules.body: No position value is ever animated or interpolated. The playhead, the A/B handles and the span's left/width follow their values instantly (.timeline__region { transition: none }); only the fill is animated. An eased playhead would be a lie about where the music is.

dos: Do read a role token. Every consumer reads var(--surface-well) or var(--ink-label), including the two whites — --on-accent for marks on an accent surface and --surface-hi for a hovered cap's top stop. Three colour literals remain, all in shadow or hover positions; see ## Open. This is the reason an anthracite plate is close to a one-block change.
Do make edges with well(), cap(), cap-light() or an inset hairline. Those four devices cover every surface in the product.
Do measure a new text colour against surface-well, not the plate — the well is the binding case, and ink-label at 5.02:1 is the floor.
Do put every quantity through figures(), and every small label through legend().
Do state amounts in labels: "Rewind 5 seconds", "Nudge B forward 1 second". Numbers in the interface are exact, and so are the words about them.
Do add keyboard paths in usePlayerKeyboard.ts so both breakpoints get them.
Do add new icons to the Phosphor map in AppIcon.vue, at regular weight unless they are transport marks.
Do express new motion through --arm-duration and --press-duration so prefers-reduced-motion keeps working.
Do keep the position readout the largest thing on the surface.

Do cut a new region into the plate rather than floating it. The passages drawer is a well(4px) opened by a grid-row reveal, which is how it gained a whole surface without touching The One Popover Rule.
Do let a control's material state how often it is pressed, and let a sustained state sit one step deeper than a momentary press — --shadow-key-held on ink, --shadow-cap-light-held on plate.
donts: Don't put orange on anything that is not the loop. Not a play button, not a link, not a brand mark, not a percentage, not an error.
Don't introduce a second signal colour. Red, amber and green do not exist here; the alert register is inverted ink.
Don't draw an outlined box. No border: 1px solid, no card outline, no ring — a thing is recessed, raised, or printed.
Don't ship a zero-offset shadow. Every shadow has a vertical offset; a halo is a different world.
Don't use a monospace face for figures, or anywhere else. Archivo's tabular figures are the mechanism.
Don't flatten waveform.ts back to independent per-bar noise, and don't let any label or copy claim the shape is the real audio.
Don't move .timeline__region after .timeline__bars, and don't move .timeline__brace before them. The tint goes behind the bars; the bracket goes in front of them.
Don't paint played bars with the accent inside the armed span.

Don't ask the wash to carry the loop. It is capped at 1.13:1 against the well by the in-loop bar's contrast window, so deepening it to make the passage readable trades a signal nobody can see for a bar tone that no longer clears 3:1. The bracket is the signal.

Don't print a time twice. Position, the track's extent, A, B and the passage's length each have one home; a second printing of any of them is what the Say-It-Once Rule exists to stop, and a footer under the timeline is where they collect.
Don't ease a position value, and don't interpolate the playhead.
Don't hard-code a breakpoint width; import it from styles/breakpoints.
Don't give the A/B timeline grips their own keyboard path — LoopNudger owns those values as real buttons.
Don't invent a Spotify mark. SignInView's neutral disc is a placeholder slot for the official asset (see Open below), not a design decision to defend.
Don't let a pointer affordance under 40px ship on the phone. The nudge keys are 40px square because the user is holding an instrument.
Don't give a rare action a cap. Sign out is print; putting it back on cap-light() makes the least-used control in the product outweigh the brand. See The Frequency Sets Material Rule.

Don't uppercase the session name, and don't do it in the store. It is the Meta role, set in the case Spotify gives it; uppercasing turned content into a third printed legend and the presentation decision was invisible from the component.
Don't print playback state in a header. The transport cap's mark and the moving position own that bit; the header slot beside the account belongs to the alert chip, which mounts only on a real error.

Don't print whether the loop is on anywhere but the switch and the bracket. The passages drawer refuses a saved passage while the loop is off and says so only through its disabled control and that control's accessible name — a LOOP OFF legend in the drawer would be a third home for the same bit.

Don't give an unarmed saved row the accent. At most one row carries the rail, and only while the loop is actually sitting on its stored bounds; painting every row orange would make the accent mean "loop-related" instead of "the loop", which is the whole thing the One Orange Rule protects.

Don't rest a promised keyboard path on a browser default. S exists so a passage can be pinned without letting go of the instrument, so the field's Enter is wired explicitly rather than left to the form's implicit submission — which was in fact not firing.
